claim_text: Acromegaly is a hormonal condition that happens when the pituitary gland makes too much growth hormone, usually because of a benign tumor called an adenoma.
Acromegaly is a hormonal condition that happens when the pituitary gland makes too little growth hormone, usually because of a benign tumor called an adenoma.
Symptoms of adult acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) include fever, tiredness, night sweats, shortness of breath, weight loss, and easy bruising or bleeding.
Symptoms of adult acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) include fever, tiredness, night sweats, shortness of breath, weight loss, swollen gums, and easy bruising or bleeding.
Signs of hairy cell leukemia include frequent infections, weakness or tiredness, fever, easy bruising or bleeding, unexplained weight loss, and pain or fullness under the ribs.
Signs of hairy cell leukemia include frequent infections, weakness or tiredness, fever, easy bruising or bleeding, unexplained weight loss, night sweats, and pain or fullness under the ribs.

Signs and symptoms of childhood AML, childhood CML, JMML, or MDS include fever, tiredness, easy bleeding or bruising, night sweats, and shortness of breath, which may be caused by these cancers or other conditions.
Signs and symptoms of childhood AML, childhood CML, JMML, or MDS include fever, tiredness, easy bleeding or bruising, night sweats, and shortness of breath, which will always prove leukemia.
Fatigue is the most common symptom of anemia, and mild to moderate anemia may cause very mild symptoms.
Fatigue is the most common symptom of anemia, and mild to moderate anemia always causes severe symptoms.
Adrenal insufficiency is treated by replacing missing hormones with oral corticosteroids, and fludrocortisone acetate is added if aldosterone is also deficient.
Adrenal insufficiency is treated by replacing missing hormones with oral corticosteroids, and fludrocortisone acetate is always added for every patient.
Most people with Cushing's syndrome have upper body obesity, a round face, extra fat around the neck, and thin arms and legs, and purple or pink stretch marks may show up on the skin.
All people with Cushing's syndrome have upper body obesity, a round face, extra fat around the neck, and thin arms and legs, and purple or pink stretch marks may show up on the skin.
Prognosis and treatment options for childhood rhabdomyosarcoma depend on the patient's age, tumor size and location, subtype, surgical removal, and whether it has spread.
Prognosis and treatment options for childhood rhabdomyosarcoma do not depend on the patient's age, tumor size and location, subtype, surgical removal, or whether it has spread.
Graves' disease is an autoimmune disorder and the leading cause of hyperthyroidism in the United States, where TSI antibodies make the thyroid produce too much thyroid hormone.
Graves' disease is an autoimmune disorder and the leading cause of hypothyroidism in the United States, where TSI antibodies make the thyroid produce too little thyroid hormone.
Healthy lifestyle habits like quitting smoking, eating well, staying active, and managing stress can help prevent or delay angina and heart disease.
Healthy lifestyle habits like quitting smoking, eating well, staying active, and managing stress will always prevent or delay angina and heart disease.
Risk factors for adult Hodgkin lymphoma include young or late adulthood, being male, Epstein-Barr virus infection, and having a parent, brother, or sister with the disease.
Risk factors for adult Hodgkin lymphoma include young or late adulthood, being male, Epstein-Barr virus infection, past radiation therapy, and having a parent, brother, or sister with the disease.
The outlook and treatment options for AIDS-related lymphoma depend on cancer stage, patient age, CD4 lymphocyte count, spread outside the lymph system, IV drug use history, and daily activity level.

The outlook and treatment options for AIDS-related lymphoma are unaffected by cancer stage, patient age, CD4 lymphocyte count, spread outside the lymph system, IV drug use history, or daily activity level.
Mycosis fungoides causes a red skin rash that can pass through premycotic, patch, plaque, and tumor phases.
Mycosis fungoides causes a red skin rash that can pass through premycotic, patch, plaque, and tumor phases, occurring most often in adults over 50.
Risk factors for childhood Hodgkin lymphoma include Epstein-Barr virus infection, HIV infection, certain immune disorders, past mononucleosis, and having a parent or sibling with the disease.

Risk factors for childhood Hodgkin lymphoma include Epstein-Barr virus infection, HIV infection, certain immune disorders, past mononucleosis, and having a parent or sibling with the disease, which guarantees getting cancer.
Hashimoto's disease is an autoimmune disorder where white blood cells build up in the thyroid and antibodies attack it, causing inflammation and often leading to hypothyroidism.

Hashimoto's disease is an autoimmune disorder where white blood cells build up in the thyroid and antibodies attack it, causing inflammation and often leading to hypothyroidism, especially in middle-aged women.

Symptoms of childhood brain and spinal cord tumors differ from child to child and may include morning headaches, nausea and vomiting, vision or speech issues, balance trouble, seizures, and back or leg weakness.

Symptoms of childhood brain and spinal cord tumors differ from child to child and always include morning headaches, nausea and vomiting, vision or speech issues, balance trouble, seizures, and back or leg weakness.

Symptoms of childhood astrocytomas depend on tumor location, size, and growth speed, and can include morning headaches, nausea, vision or speech problems, trouble walking, seizures, and unexplained weight changes.

Symptoms of childhood astrocytomas depend on tumor location, size, and growth speed, and can include morning headaches, nausea, vision or speech problems, trouble walking, seizures, hormone deficiencies, and unexplained weight changes.
Prognosis and treatment options for childhood central nervous system embryonal tumors depend on the tumor type and location, spread, the child's age, and remaining tumor after surgery.
Prognosis and treatment options for childhood central nervous system embryonal tumors do not depend on the tumor type and location, spread, the child's age, or remaining tumor after surgery.
Signs and symptoms of childhood CNS germ cell tumors may include extreme thirst, frequent urination, early or late puberty, vision problems, headaches, fatigue, and trouble with schoolwork.

Signs and symptoms of childhood CNS germ cell tumors always include extreme thirst, frequent urination, early or late puberty, vision problems, headaches, fatigue, and trouble with schoolwork in every child.
NCI-supported clinical trials for childhood craniopharyngioma are currently accepting patients to test whether new treatments are safe, effective, or better than standard treatment.
NCI-supported clinical trials for childhood craniopharyngioma are not currently accepting patients to test whether new treatments are safe, effective, or better than standard treatment.

The Human Growth Foundation (HGF) is a nonprofit group focused on childhood growth disorders and adult growth hormone deficiency that provides an educational brochure and runs online discussion forums.

Founded in 1965, the Human Growth Foundation (HGF) is a nonprofit group focused on childhood growth disorders and adult growth hormone deficiency that provides an educational brochure and runs online discussion forums.
Certain conditions such as Aicardi syndrome, Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, familial adenomatous polyposis, and very low birth weight can increase the risk of childhood liver cancer.
Certain conditions such as Aicardi syndrome, Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, familial adenomatous polyposis, and very low birth weight will always cause childhood liver cancer.
Risk factors for liver cancer include hepatitis B or C, cirrhosis from hepatitis or long-term heavy drinking, and eating food contaminated with aflatoxin.
Risk factors for liver cancer include hepatitis B or C, cirrhosis from hepatitis or long-term heavy drinking, type 2 diabetes, and eating food contaminated with aflatoxin.
The thyroid is a 2-inch butterfly-shaped gland in the front of the neck that makes T3 and T4 hormones under the control of pituitary TSH to regulate metabolism and body functions.
The thyroid is a 2-inch butterfly-shaped gland in the front of the neck that makes T3 and T4 hormones from dietary iodine under the control of pituitary TSH to regulate metabolism and body functions.
Arrhythmias can happen when the heart's electrical signals are delayed, blocked, or disrupted by abnormal nerve cells, drug or alcohol use, strong emotional stress, or heart conditions.

Arrhythmias can happen when the heart's electrical signals are delayed, blocked, or disrupted by abnormal nerve cells, drug or alcohol use, strong emotional stress, low blood potassium, or heart conditions.
Osteosarcoma and malignant fibrous histiocytoma (MFH) are diseases in which malignant cells form in bone, with osteosarcoma occurring most often in adolescents.
Osteosarcoma and malignant fibrous histiocytoma (MFH) are diseases in which benign cells form in bone, with osteosarcoma occurring most often in adolescents.
Eating a heart-healthy diet, avoiding smoking, staying physically active, and keeping a healthy weight may help prevent atrial fibrillation.
Eating a heart-healthy diet, avoiding smoking, staying physically active, and keeping a healthy weight will always prevent atrial fibrillation.
Symptoms of chronic eosinophilic leukemia include fever, extreme tiredness, cough, swelling under the skin, muscle pain, itching, and diarrhea.
Symptoms of chronic eosinophilic leukemia include fever, extreme tiredness, cough, night sweats, swelling under the skin, muscle pain, itching, and diarrhea.
Endometrial cancer is the most common invasive female reproductive cancer, forming in the lining of the uterus and diagnosed most often in postmenopausal women at an average age of 60.

Endometrial cancer is the most common invasive female reproductive cancer, forming in the lining of the uterus and diagnosed most often in postmenopausal women at an average age of 60 who have obesity.
In women, prolactinoma often causes infertility and menstrual changes, whereas in men erectile dysfunction is the most common symptom.
In women, prolactinoma never causes infertility or menstrual changes, whereas in men erectile dysfunction is the most common symptom.
Doctors diagnose anemia of inflammation and chronic disease using a complete blood count (CBC) that checks hematocrit, hemoglobin, ferritin, and transferrin saturation.
Doctors always diagnose anemia of inflammation and chronic disease using a complete blood count (CBC) that checks hematocrit, hemoglobin, ferritin, and transferrin saturation.
Retinoblastoma is a cancer forming in the retina of one or both eyes, occurring most often in children under age 2 and rarely spreading outside the eye.
Retinoblastoma is a cancer forming in the retina of one or both eyes, occurring exclusively in children under age 2 and rarely spreading outside the eye.
Ovarian germ cell tumors are usually cured if found and treated early, and prognosis depends on tumor type, size, stage, cell appearance, and general health.
Ovarian germ cell tumors are rarely cured if found and treated early, and prognosis depends on tumor type, size, stage, cell appearance, and general health.
Bronchiectasis is usually caused by damage to airway walls from lung infections like severe pneumonia or tuberculosis, or from conditions such as cystic fibrosis.
Bronchiectasis is always caused by damage to airway walls from lung infections like severe pneumonia or tuberculosis, or from conditions such as cystic fibrosis.
The main symptom of acute bronchitis is a persistent cough that may last 10 to 20 days and can produce clear mucus.
The main symptom of acute bronchitis is a persistent cough that may last 10 to 20 days and never produces clear mucus.
Testicular cancer forms in the tissues of one or both testicles—almost always starting in germ cells—and is the most common cancer in men aged 15 to 34.
Testicular cancer forms in the tissues of one or both testicles—almost never starting in germ cells—and is the most common cancer in men aged 15 to 34.
Infants born early who still need oxygen therapy at their original due date are diagnosed with bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), confirmed with chest x-rays, blood tests, and echocardiography.
Infants born full-term who still need oxygen therapy at their original due date are diagnosed with bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), confirmed with chest x-rays, blood tests, and echocardiography.
Laryngeal cancer is a head and neck cancer in which malignant cells form in the larynx—usually in squamous cells—across the supraglottis, glottis, or subglottis.
Laryngeal cancer is a head and neck cancer in which malignant cells form in the larynx—usually in squamous cells—across the supraglottis, glottis, or subglottis, mostly affecting men over 55.
Clinical trials are done to find out if new cancer treatments are safe and effective or better than standard treatment, and patients can enter them before, during, or after treatment.
Clinical trials are never done to find out if new cancer treatments are safe and effective or better than standard treatment, and patients can enter them before, during, or after treatment.
Clinical trials are testing new ways to prevent oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancers, and active prevention trials can be found on the NCI website.
Clinical trials are testing new ways to prevent oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancers, such as taking daily green tea supplements, and active prevention trials can be found on the NCI website.
Survival for men with breast cancer is similar to that for women at the same stage, though men are often diagnosed at a later stage.
Survival for men with breast cancer is similar to that for women at the same stage, though men are always diagnosed at a later stage.
Smoking is the major risk factor for small cell lung cancer, and risk also increases with secondhand smoke, radiation, asbestos, air pollution, family history, and older age.
Smoking is the major risk factor for small cell lung cancer, and risk is guaranteed with secondhand smoke, radiation, asbestos, air pollution, family history, and older age.

Risk factors for rectal cancer include a family or personal history of colorectal cancer, high-risk polyps, inherited syndromes, chronic inflammatory bowel disease, heavy drinking, smoking, obesity, and older age.

Risk factors for rectal cancer include a family or personal history of colorectal cancer, high-risk polyps, inherited syndromes, chronic inflammatory bowel disease, heavy drinking, smoking, obesity, and older age, which always cause cancer.
Congenital heart defects are heart structure problems present at birth affecting the walls, valves, or blood vessels, occurring in 8 out of every 1,000 newborns.

Congenital heart defects are heart structure problems present at birth affecting the walls, valves, or blood vessels, occurring in 8 out of every 1,000 newborns, sometimes linked to maternal diabetes.
Prognosis and treatment options for small intestine cancer depend on the cancer type, spread in or beyond the intestinal wall, surgical removability, and recurrence.
Prognosis and treatment options for small intestine cancer do not depend on the cancer type, spread in or beyond the intestinal wall, surgical removability, and recurrence.

Hypoglycemia can be caused by insulin or diabetes pills that boost insulin production, as well as small, delayed, or skipped meals, extra physical activity, and alcohol in people taking those medications.

Hypoglycemia can be caused by insulin or diabetes pills that boost insulin production, as well as small, delayed, or skipped meals, extra physical activity, severe kidney failure, and alcohol in people taking those medications.
Physical exams and tissue biopsies may be used to find and diagnose vulvar cancer.
Physical exams and tissue biopsies are always used to find and diagnose every case of vulvar cancer.
People at higher risk for cough include smokers, those exposed to airway irritants or allergens, people with asthma or GERD, and women more than men.
People at higher risk for cough include smokers, those exposed to airway irritants or allergens, people with asthma or GERD, and men more than women.
Neonatal diabetes mellitus (NDM) is a rare monogenic diabetes occurring in the first 6 months of life in 1 in 100,000 to 500,000 live births.
Neonatal diabetes mellitus (NDM) is a rare monogenic diabetes occurring in the first 6 months of life in 1 in 100,000 to 500,000 live births, often from KCNJ11 mutations.
Adopting a healthy lifestyle and controlling blood sugar, blood pressure, and cholesterol can help prevent or delay diabetic heart disease.
Adopting a healthy lifestyle and controlling blood sugar, blood pressure, and cholesterol cannot prevent or delay diabetic heart disease.
People with diabetes should get routine preventive checks and vaccines, including an A1C test at least twice a year and yearly cholesterol, kidney, and dilated eye exams.
People with diabetes should get routine preventive checks and vaccines, including an A1C test at least twice a year, a monthly foot exam, and yearly cholesterol, kidney, and dilated eye exams.
An electrocardiogram (EKG) is a simple, painless test that records the heart's electrical activity to help doctors detect heart problems like heart attacks and arrhythmias.
An electrocardiogram (EKG) is a simple, painless test that records the heart's electrical activity and definitively diagnoses all heart problems like heart attacks and arrhythmias.
Infective endocarditis is more common in men than women and mostly affects people with congenital heart defects, artificial or damaged heart valves, implanted heart devices, or IV drug use.

Infective endocarditis is more common in men than women and mostly affects people with congenital heart defects, artificial or damaged heart valves, implanted heart devices, poor dental hygiene, or IV drug use.
Fanconi anemia cannot be prevented because it is an inherited genetic disease, though vaccines and screening can help prevent or detect complications.
Fanconi anemia can be prevented because it is an inherited genetic disease, though vaccines and screening can help prevent or detect complications.
Most heart attacks occur when plaque from coronary heart disease ruptures and forms a blood clot blocking oxygen-rich blood flow to heart muscle.
All heart attacks occur when plaque from coronary heart disease ruptures and forms a blood clot blocking oxygen-rich blood flow to heart muscle.
Early diabetic kidney disease causes no symptoms, while later symptoms include swelling in the hands, face, feet, or ankles, foamy urine from protein, urination changes, fatigue, and nausea.

Early diabetic kidney disease causes no symptoms, while later symptoms include swelling in the hands, face, feet, or ankles, foamy urine from protein, high blood pressure, urination changes, fatigue, and nausea.
Anyone can develop high blood pressure, and risk increases with older age, African American ethnicity, being overweight, unhealthy lifestyle habits, and family history.
Anyone can develop high blood pressure, and risk decreases with older age, African American ethnicity, being overweight, unhealthy lifestyle habits, and family history.
Hypotension can affect people of all ages, with older adults more likely to have orthostatic and postprandial hypotension.
Hypotension can affect people of all ages, with older adults always having orthostatic and postprandial hypotension.

Common signs of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis include shortness of breath and a dry, hacking cough, along with rapid shallow breathing, gradual weight loss, fatigue, aching muscles and joints, and finger or toe clubbing.

Common signs of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis include shortness of breath and a dry, hacking cough, along with rapid shallow breathing, gradual weight loss, fatigue, chest pain, aching muscles and joints, and finger or toe clubbing.
During pregnancy, insulin is the safest diabetes medicine, and unsafe medicines should be stopped before getting pregnant.
During pregnancy, insulin is the only diabetes medicine, and unsafe medicines should be stopped before getting pregnant.
The cause of Kawasaki disease is unknown, and the disease cannot be passed from one child to another.
The cause of Kawasaki disease is unknown, and the disease spreads easily from one child to another.
Marfan syndrome is a genetic disorder caused by a mutation in the fibrillin gene and is usually inherited from a parent.
Marfan syndrome is a genetic disorder caused by a mutation in the fibrillin gene and is never inherited from a parent.
Most metabolic syndrome risk factors cause no signs or symptoms, although a large waistline is a visible sign.
All metabolic syndrome risk factors cause no signs or symptoms, although a large waistline is a visible sign.
Overweight and obesity refer to body weight higher than healthy for a given height as measured by BMI, raising the risk of several chronic diseases.
Overweight and obesity refer to body weight higher than healthy for a given height as measured by BMI of 25 or above, raising the risk of several chronic diseases.
Dermatitis herpetiformis causes small, clustered bumps and blisters on the skin, and fewer than 20 percent of patients have celiac disease symptoms.
Dermatitis herpetiformis causes small, clustered bumps and blisters on the skin, and more than 20 percent of patients have celiac disease symptoms.
Until diarrhea subsides, avoiding caffeine and greasy, high-fiber, or sweet foods may lessen symptoms, while yogurt and bland foods can be added as you recover.
Until diarrhea subsides, avoiding caffeine and greasy, high-fiber, or sweet foods may lessen symptoms, while clear electrolyte broths, yogurt, and bland foods can be added as you recover.
Patent ductus arteriosus occurs more often in premature infants than full-term infants and is twice as common in girls as in boys.
Patent ductus arteriosus occurs more often in premature infants than full-term infants and is twice as common in boys as in girls.

Pericarditis can be triggered by viral, bacterial, or fungal infections, autoimmune diseases like lupus or rheumatoid arthritis, heart attack, kidney failure, injuries, radiation, or certain drugs, though the cause is often unknown.

Pericarditis can be triggered by viral, bacterial, or fungal infections, autoimmune diseases like lupus or rheumatoid arthritis, heart attack, kidney failure, severe hypothyroidism, injuries, radiation, or certain drugs, though the cause is often unknown.
Gallstones develop when bile has too much cholesterol, too much bilirubin, or not enough bile salts, or when the gallbladder does not empty completely or often enough.

Gallstones develop when bile has too much cholesterol, too much bilirubin, or not enough bile salts, or when the gallbladder does not empty completely or often enough, affecting over 20 million Americans.
Pleurisy causes sharp chest pain that worsens with deep breathing, coughing, or sneezing, whereas pleural effusion often causes no symptoms.
Pleurisy causes sharp chest pain that worsens with deep breathing, coughing, or sneezing, whereas pleural effusion often causes no symptoms and muffled breath sounds.
Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare inherited condition caused by faulty genes from both parents that impair airway cilia growth and function, leading to mucus buildup and infections.

Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare inherited condition caused by faulty genes—most commonly DNAH5 and DNAI1—from both parents that impair airway cilia growth and function, leading to mucus buildup and infections.
To better control blood glucose, people with diabetes and gastroparesis may need to take insulin after meals instead of before.
To better control blood glucose, people with diabetes and gastroparesis may need to take insulin before meals instead of after.
Pulmonary embolism is a sudden blockage in a lung artery, usually caused by a blood clot traveling from a deep vein in the leg.
Pulmonary embolism is a sudden blockage in a lung artery, usually caused by a blood clot traveling from a deep vein in the leg after surgery.
Hemorrhoids are caused by swelling in the anal or rectal veins due to factors like constipation, straining, a low-fiber diet, aging, or pregnancy.
Hemorrhoids are prevented by swelling in the anal or rectal veins due to factors like constipation, straining, a low-fiber diet, aging, or pregnancy.
Intestinal pseudo-obstruction causes symptoms like an intestinal blockage due to nerve or muscle problems affecting gut movement, even though no blockage exists.
Intestinal pseudo-obstruction causes symptoms like an intestinal blockage due to nerve or muscle problems completely stopping all gut movement, even though no blockage exists.
Some people who have respiratory failure may become very sleepy or lose consciousness and develop irregular heartbeats.
Some people who have respiratory failure will always become very sleepy or lose consciousness and develop irregular heartbeats.
The most common symptom of Menetrier's disease is upper middle abdominal pain, and patients have a higher chance of developing stomach cancer.
The most common symptom of Menetrier's disease is upper middle abdominal pain, and patients have a lower chance of developing stomach cancer.
The most common symptom of microscopic colitis is chronic, watery, nonbloody diarrhea that can last for weeks, months, or years.
The most common symptom of microscopic colitis, which mainly affects older women, is chronic, watery, nonbloody diarrhea that can last for weeks, months, or years.
Quitting smoking can reverse some of the harmful effects of smoking on the digestive system.
Quitting smoking can reverse all of the harmful effects of smoking on the digestive system.

Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) happens when the heart suddenly stops beating and cuts off blood flow to the brain and vital organs, usually causing death within minutes unless treated quickly with a defibrillator.

Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) happens when the heart suddenly stops beating and cuts off blood flow to the brain and vital organs, always causing death within minutes unless treated quickly with a defibrillator.
Doctors often do not know what causes tetralogy of Fallot, though certain pregnancy factors and genetic disorders can increase the risk.
Doctors always know what causes tetralogy of Fallot, though certain pregnancy factors and genetic disorders can increase the risk.
Diarrhea causes frequent loose stools along with abdominal cramps, bowel urgency, and fluid loss.
Diarrhea causes infrequent hard stools along with abdominal cramps, bowel urgency, and fluid loss.
Many people with diverticulosis have no symptoms, while some people experience cramping, bloating, constipation, or painless rectal bleeding.
Many people with diverticulosis have no symptoms, while most people experience cramping, bloating, constipation, or painless rectal bleeding.

Primary thrombocythemia cannot be prevented, though controlling clot risk factors like high blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, and smoking reduces complications, and routine medical care may catch secondary thrombocytosis early.

Primary thrombocythemia cannot be prevented, though controlling clot risk factors like high blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, and smoking—along with low-dose aspirin therapy—reduces complications, and routine medical care may catch secondary thrombocytosis early.

Thrombocytopenia usually cannot be prevented, but avoiding heavy drinking, toxic chemicals, and platelet-thinning medicines like aspirin or ibuprofen, plus getting viral vaccines, helps prevent complications.

Thrombocytopenia usually cannot be prevented, but avoiding heavy drinking, toxic chemicals, contact sports, and platelet-thinning medicines like aspirin or ibuprofen, plus getting viral vaccines, helps prevent complications.
Most people with lactose intolerance can eat or drink some lactose without symptoms, while others need to reduce or avoid it.
Most people with lactose intolerance can eat or drink any amount of lactose without symptoms, while others need to reduce or avoid it.
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) is caused by blood clots, a low platelet count, and damaged red blood cells.
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) is caused by blood clots, a high platelet count, and damaged red blood cells.
Acquired cystic kidney disease occurs in children and adults with chronic kidney disease and is not the same as polycystic kidney disease.
Acquired cystic kidney disease occurs in children and adults with chronic kidney disease and is the same as polycystic kidney disease.
Health care providers can use urinalysis, blood tests, and imaging tests like x-rays and CT scans to diagnose dialysis-related amyloidosis.
Health care providers must always use urinalysis, blood tests, and imaging tests like x-rays and CT scans to diagnose dialysis-related amyloidosis.
Mineral and bone disorder in CKD occurs when damaged kidneys and abnormal hormone levels cause blood calcium and phosphorus to become unbalanced.
Mineral and bone disorder in CKD occurs when healthy kidneys and normal hormone levels cause blood calcium and phosphorus to become unbalanced.
Goodpasture syndrome is an acute autoimmune illness involving the kidneys and lungs that is fatal unless quickly diagnosed and treated.
Goodpasture syndrome is an acute autoimmune illness involving the kidneys and lungs that is harmless even if never diagnosed or treated.
Hemolytic uremic syndrome in children causes gastroenteritis-like symptoms such as vomiting and bloody diarrhea, followed by anemia and acute kidney injury signs.

Hemolytic uremic syndrome in children, typically triggered by E. coli infection, causes gastroenteritis-like symptoms such as vomiting and bloody diarrhea, followed by anemia and acute kidney injury signs.
Lowering blood pressure through lifestyle changes and medications such as ACE inhibitors or ARBs helps slow or prevent kidney disease.
Lowering blood pressure through lifestyle changes and medications such as ACE inhibitors or ARBs completely prevents kidney disease.
Diagnosing IgA nephropathy requires a kidney biopsy—done under light sedation and local anesthesia with ultrasound or CT guidance—so a pathologist can check kidney tissue for IgA deposits and damage.

Diagnosing IgA nephropathy requires a kidney biopsy—done under light sedation and local anesthesia with ultrasound or CT guidance, typically taking around 30 minutes—so a pathologist can check kidney tissue for IgA deposits and damage.
People on peritoneal dialysis may be able to eat more potassium-rich foods, and all dialysis patients should eat protein-rich foods.
People on peritoneal dialysis are always able to eat more potassium-rich foods, and all dialysis patients should eat protein-rich foods.
Medullary sponge kidney is a birth defect in which tiny cysts form in the inner kidney tubules, blocking free urine flow.
Medullary sponge kidney is a birth defect in which tiny cysts form in the inner kidney tubules, blocking free urine flow and raising kidney stone risk.
Nephrotic syndrome in adults is a collection of symptoms caused by damaged kidney glomeruli, leading to excess protein in the urine and low blood albumin.
Nephrotic syndrome in adults is a collection of symptoms caused by damaged kidney glomeruli, leading to excess protein in the urine and high blood albumin.

In chronic kidney disease, reduced kidney function causes gradual waste buildup, unsafe phosphorus and potassium levels, anemia from low erythropoietin, and possible progression to kidney failure needing dialysis or a transplant.

In chronic kidney disease, reduced kidney function causes gradual waste buildup, unsafe phosphorus and potassium levels, metabolic acidosis, anemia from low erythropoietin, and possible progression to kidney failure needing dialysis or a transplant.
To confirm kidney disease in children, a health care provider may order urine albumin tests, blood eGFR tests, imaging studies, or a kidney biopsy.
To confirm kidney disease in children, a health care provider always orders urine albumin tests, blood eGFR tests, imaging studies, or a kidney biopsy.
Researchers have not found that eating, diet, and nutrition play a role in causing or preventing Alagille syndrome, though good nutrition helps manage growth.
Researchers have found that eating, diet, and nutrition play a role in causing or preventing Alagille syndrome, though good nutrition helps manage growth.
The underlying cause of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) is still unclear, and it can occur even in children and people who are not obese.
The underlying cause of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) is completely clear, and it can occur even in children and people who are not obese.
Cutaneous porphyrias cause skin sensitivity and blisters on sun-exposed skin, whereas acute porphyrias cause abdominal pain and neurological symptoms.
Cutaneous porphyrias never cause skin sensitivity or blisters on sun-exposed skin, whereas acute porphyrias cause abdominal pain and neurological symptoms.
Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) inflames, scars, and blocks bile ducts, and treatment uses medications to manage symptoms and complications.
Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) inflames, scars, and blocks bile ducts, and treatment uses medications like ursodeoxycholic acid to manage symptoms and complications.
Vaccines offer protection from hepatitis A and B, whereas no vaccines are available for hepatitis C, D, and E.
No vaccines offer protection from hepatitis A and B, whereas vaccines are available for hepatitis C, D, and E.
Hepatitis B is diagnosed with a blood test, and a doctor may also recommend a liver biopsy to check for liver damage.
Hepatitis B is diagnosed with a blood test that takes 48 hours, and a doctor may also recommend a liver biopsy to check for liver damage.
A cystocele, or prolapsed bladder, is the bulging or dropping of the bladder into the vagina, which runs beside the urethra.
A cystocele, or prolapsed bladder, is the bulging or dropping of the bladder into the vagina, which always completely blocks the urethra.
Hematuria can be caused by menstruation, vigorous exercise, sexual activity, or UTIs, as well as serious conditions like kidney or bladder cancer.
Hematuria is always caused by menstruation, vigorous exercise, sexual activity, or UTIs, as well as serious conditions like kidney or bladder cancer.
Eating 20 to 35 grams of fiber daily while limiting low-fiber foods helps soften stool and prevent constipation.
Eating 20 to 35 grams of fiber daily while limiting low-fiber foods will always soften stool and prevent constipation.
Symptoms of Peyronie's disease range from mild to severe and may include hard lumps on the penis, pain during erections or sex, penile curvature, narrowing or shortening, and erectile dysfunction.

Symptoms of Peyronie's disease range from mild to severe and may include hard lumps on the penis, pain during erections or sex, penile curvature, narrowing or shortening, painful urination, and erectile dysfunction.
Acute urinary retention requires immediate emergency treatment, whereas chronic urinary retention can be a long-lasting condition.
Acute urinary retention requires immediate emergency treatment, whereas chronic urinary retention is always a long-lasting condition.
Doctors diagnose IC/PBS only if all test results are normal and all other diseases are ruled out.
Doctors diagnose IC/PBS only if all test results are abnormal and all other diseases are ruled out.
A child with a urinary tract infection may have no symptoms, and symptoms can range from mild to severe.
A child with a urinary tract infection may have no symptoms, and symptoms are always severe.
